lines: Once Telo Ride has been opened, it opens again with no network, and a solo race starts.
Angular's service worker keeps the app on the device: every script at once, map art and worlds the first time they are seen.
Offline, the race comes from the cache, the maps from the catalogue the app keeps, and the rider's progress from its last answer.
A map cover seen once still shows with no network, so Map Select looks as it did.
The worker registers from the first screen's lazy chunk, so the first bundle grows by forty bytes, not six kilobytes.
The offline race, from a phone to the full screen.
What the tests prove: opened once, the app opens offline, a solo race starts, and the covers still show.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
